question: Should the unique delayed-sentinel and late-sidecar changes be rebased into a narrow current-main patch, or is this branch now fully superseded by the queue-owned recovery runtime?
rationale: The central retry behavior now exists in a substantially evolved current-main architecture, while the remaining branch changes touch shutdown and at-least-once delivery semantics and cannot be safely carried forward wholesale.

options.title: Port the unique invariants
options.body: Rebase or replace this branch with only the still-missing sentinel and sidecar lifecycle fixes, including an awaited in-flight recovery contract and fresh proof.

options.title: Close as superseded
options.body: Close after confirming current main already contains equivalent sentinel removal and late-sidecar shutdown guarantees in addition to its queue-owned scheduler.

recommendation.title: Port the unique invariants
recommendation.body: Rebase or replace this branch with only the still-missing sentinel and sidecar lifecycle fixes, including an awaited in-flight recovery contract and fresh proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They reviewed the shutdown lifecycle defects on this PR and are the clearest available routing owner for deciding whether the remaining invariants belong on current main.
